summary: The Blocking Large-scale Adversarial Distillation Efforts Act of 2026, or the BLADE Act, directs the federal government to assess, identify, and deter unauthorized attempts by foreign adversaries to extract key technical features from proprietary, closed-source artificial intelligence models owned by United States entities.

affected_groups.effect: May voluntarily participate in consultations, share information confidentially with the Department of Commerce, and receive government assistance in detecting and deterring attacks.
affected_groups.group: U.S. owners of closed-source AI models

affected_groups.effect: Subject to federal assessments, inclusion on a public attackers list, placement on the Entity List, and asset-blocking economic sanctions.
affected_groups.group: Foreign persons of concern and fraudulent account network providers

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Commerce to complete an initial assessment within 180 days to identify foreign persons of concern conducting model extraction attacks or operating fraudulent account networks.
Establishes an information-sharing mechanism for U.S. owners of closed-source AI models to confidentially report attacks to the Department of Commerce.
Requires the creation and public publication of an 'AI Model Extraction Attackers List' of specific persons of concern who have directed model extraction attacks.
Mandates the publication of public guidance and best practices to detect, prevent, and respond to model extraction attacks.
Requires the addition of identified entities and their 50-percent-or-more owned subsidiaries to the Bureau of Industry and Security's Entity List.

Directs the President to block and prohibit all U.S. property and property transactions of identified persons of concern under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, subject to specific humanitarian and national security exceptions.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Blocking Large-scale Adversarial Distillation Efforts Act of 2026, or the BLADE Act, directs the federal government to assess, identify, and deter unauthorized attempts by foreign adversaries to extract key technical features from proprietary, closed-source artificial intelligence models owned by United States entities.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a formal federal mechanism to protect domestic artificial intelligence intellectual property and national security by investigating and penalizing foreign entities that use unauthorized methods to replicate U.S.-owned closed-source AI models.
